nodes.title: Finite controlled predictive quotient and exact linear rank dimension
nodes.claim: At a registered finite horizon and finite complete test block, predictive-row equivalence is exact predictive sufficiency; the minimum exact linear predictive dimension equals the rank of the system-dynamics matrix.
premises: linear predictive representation reconstructs every registered test probability
nodes.inference: #846 PS-1 supplies quotient sufficiency/minimality; rank factorization gives rank(D) <= d for any exact d-dimensional linear representation and an exact rank(D)-dimensional core-test construction.
nodes.unresolved_assumption: Only the finite exact block is closed; no finite-sample learning, approximation, infinite-horizon, or causal latent identification follows.
nodes.possible_counterexample: An exact d-dimensional linear representation exists with d < rank(D), or a chosen rank-sized core-test matrix fails to reconstruct D.
nodes.falsifier: A registered exact counterexample violates the rank bound/factorization or the receipt fails deterministic reconstruction.

nodes.title: Infinite-horizon / measurable predictive-state theory
nodes.claim: Extend the finite exact quotient/rank block to general measurable controlled stochastic processes and infinite test families.
premises: appropriate measurable-space, regular-conditional-probability, and infinite-horizon assumptions
nodes.inference: Not established by the finite matrix theorem.
nodes.unresolved_assumption: Existence/measurability/canonicality of predictive state under infinite test families remains open.
nodes.possible_counterexample: Finite-horizon predictive equality fails to determine an infinite-horizon law or a measurable quotient is ill-defined.
nodes.falsifier: A claimed extension lacks a well-defined measurable predictive statistic or changes under equivalent finite truncations.

nodes.title: Approximate predictive equivalence and error propagation
nodes.claim: Define approximate predictive equivalence and prove quantitative value/behavior error guarantees under a declared metric.
nodes.inference: Exact row equality and exact rank do not supply approximate guarantees.
nodes.unresolved_assumption: No approximation metric or error-propagation theorem is registered.
nodes.possible_counterexample: Small predictive-row error causes large downstream decision/value error under an unstable target.
nodes.falsifier: Approximate merging violates the claimed downstream guarantee.

nodes.title: Finite-sample identification of predictive state and rank
nodes.claim: Estimate predictive quotient/rank/core tests from finite stochastic data with valid error rates and abstention.
nodes.inference: Exact known probabilities do not imply learnability or finite-sample consistency/rates.
nodes.unresolved_assumption: No finite-sample estimator, rate, or confidence region is proved.
nodes.possible_counterexample: Distinct predictive rows/ranks are statistically indistinguishable at the claimed sample size.
nodes.falsifier: Claimed confidence/rate fails under a registered stochastic process satisfying its premises.

nodes.title: Causal latent-state identification beyond predictive equivalence
nodes.claim: Identify latent mechanism/state from observable controlled predictions under explicit causal/interventional assumptions.
nodes.inference: LAT-1 shows observable predictive equality alone is insufficient.
nodes.unresolved_assumption: No causal assumptions sufficient for latent identification are supplied by #836.
nodes.possible_counterexample: Two non-isomorphic latent controlled models remain interventionally/predictively indistinguishable under the registered access pattern.
nodes.falsifier: Distinct latent models satisfy all assumptions yet induce identical observable/interventional laws.
